content.text: No exclusivity obligation binds PB anywhere; the only exclusivity covenant runs against SFJ in our favour.

input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement is Section 3.19, which binds SFJ (and its Affiliates) not to develop or sell Competing Products during the defined Exclusive Period (Section 1.1.68) — an exclusivity granted in our favour, which the rule expressly treats as acceptable. There is no "sole supplier", requirements-purchase, or non-procurement obligation on PB: searches for sole supplier / requirements / procure-from-third-party language return nothing, and no mirror-image PB exclusivity commitment exists. The Approved CRO / Approved Vendor construct in Sections 2.4.1–2.4.3 is mutual and simply channels trial subcontracting through Exhibit B/C or JDC approval; it does not require PB to buy from SFJ or bar PB from using other suppliers. Section 7.5.5 (Licensing Transaction consent gate) is a financing-style covenant on out-licensing the Product, not exclusive dealing, and it carries an Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out plus expedited arbitration; it is noted here but belongs to the licensing/assignment restrictions rule rather than this one. Accordingly this sits at the preferred position — no exclusivity obligation on the Customer — and no redline is warranted.
